chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamza — he said:
I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about still water in which there is a carcass: is it proper to perform istinja' from it?
So he replied: Perform wudu from the other side, and do not perform wudu from the side of the carcass.

key_terms.الِاسْتِنْجَاءُ: istinja' — ritual cleansing of the private parts after relieving oneself
key_terms.الْجَانِبِ الْآخَرِ: the other side — spatial distancing from the point of contamination as a practical purity ruling
key_terms.الْجِيفَةُ: carcass/carrion — a source of najasah (ritual impurity) in Islamic law
key_terms.الْمَاءِ السَّاكِنِ: still/stagnant water — in Shia fiqh, more susceptible to impurity than flowing water; rules differ from kur water

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia Islam on using stagnant water containing a carcass for wudu or istinja'?
ai.summary: This hadith records a jurisprudential question put to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding stagnant water containing a carcass and its fitness for ritual purification. The Imam's ruling permits wudu from the far side of the water body while prohibiting use of the contaminated side, reflecting a practical spatial approach to managing najasah in still water. Notably, the question concerns istinja' but the Imam answers in terms of wudu, implying the ruling covers both and extends to all ritual use.
